messages:
morgan: Quick triage 1: brought up shortvec-7B int4 on the short-query holdout and saw recall@1 drop ~12ppt vs fp16. recall@10 almost identical. posting logs/commands.

devansh: ouch. paste the eval invocation and a diff table pls.

morgan: ran: `python eval.py --model shortvec-7B --quant int4 --holdout short_queries_v3 --k 1,10 --norm l2 --seed 42`

morgan: baseline fp16 (10k queries) -> R@1 0.68, R@10 0.86; int4 -> R@1 0.56, R@10 0.84

jia: Hm. Top-1 sensitive. Could be small cosine perturbations pushing correct doc to rank 2. Did you check cosine deltas for positive pairs?

morgan: yes. mean delta ~= -0.007, but tail for high-sim pairs has spikes ~ -0.02. attaching notebook screenshots to onboarding doc.

anya: possible culprits: per-tensor quant vs per-channel, or bias correction. What backend + config used?

morgan: `quantize_backend=fastq`, `per_channel=false` (default).

devansh: try per_channel=true and aq bias correction if available. Also run with/without whitening and with/without post-norm to isolate stage introducing shift.

morgan: kicking off three quick runs:
```
1) python eval.py --model shortvec-7B --quant int4 --per_channel true --holdout short_queries_v3 --k 1,10 --norm l2 --seed 42
2) python eval.py --model shortvec-7B --quant int4 --per_channel true --holdout short_queries_v3 --k 1,10 --norm none --seed 42
3) python eval.py --model shortvec-7B --quant int4 --per_channel true --apply_whitening true --holdout short_queries_v3 --k 1,10 --norm l2 --seed 42
```

eval-bot: job queued: eval-4299998888-1 (per_channel true, norm l2) 1 ETA ~7m. job queued: eval-4299998888-2 (per_channel true, norm none) 1 ETA ~8m. job queued: eval-4299998888-3 (per_channel true, whitening true) 1 ETA ~9m.

morgan: note: prod inference adds explicit L2 normalize after pooling; double-check client pipeline for duplicate normalizes.

jia: yep we had a prior incident where microbatch kv-trim changed pooled magnitudes for short contexts. worth checking.

eval-bot: eval-4299998888-1 done: R@1 0.63 (+7ppt vs int4-baseline), R@10 0.85. eval-4299998888-2 done: R@1 0.57, R@10 0.84. eval-4299998888-3 done: R@1 0.66, R@10 0.85.

devansh: nice. per-channel quant + whitening recovers most of the top-1 gap. that implies quant granularity + centering are the main drivers.

anya: can you produce quick QC slides: cosine CDFs and delta histograms for fp16 vs int4 runs, plus per-slice R@1 for query length <8 vs >=8? We'll need this to justify infra default change.

morgan: on it. plan: propose per_channel=true as canary default for shortvec family, run 10% dedicated canary and monitor R@1 and p99 latency. will add slices for short queries and multi-turn.

ops-bot: scheduled canary 2026-04-02T15:30Z on rdw-ded-3 routing 10% traffic to int4-perchannel variant.

devansh: also run multi-seed (3 seeds) to ensure this isn't seed noise. i'll take that.

jia: i'll audit client normalization calls and confirm prod does single explicit normalize.

morgan: assigned follow-ups: anya -> infra change request for default quant config; devansh -> multi-seed stress; jia -> client norm audit. pushed QC draft to https://redwood.internal/embeddings/onboard/shortvec-7B/int4-qc

anya: ack.

jia: ack.

morgan: thanks all, will update with canary metrics once live. :thumbsup:
